claim: Once a 7-Eleven-hot-dog-for-breakfast guy who didn't exercise, absolutely miserable, eating complete toxic nonsense, then a journey from about as low as you can get physically, mentally and emotionally, at least as it felt, to the strongest and best ever, at almost 40

Of the many ways to fuel your body, intermittent fasting, discovered just a few years ago, personally transformed health and fitness more than any other, and seems to have made the very most impact on life, body and mind too
Intermittent fasting came after years of trial and error with so many things nutritionally, first to lose fat and look a little better while overweight, then to feel better, be in shape and be strong

For years of training, in pretty decent shape, ideas from various sources meant eating all the time, every two hours or whatever, and reaching 11 or 12 or one o'clock unfed brought almost a guilty feeling: "oh man, I should have eaten". Then, as it was kind of just working, without real hunger, came rolling with it, and the eating period kept shrinking. Intermittent fasting, less known then, was personally not even heard of, nor were its benefits known: it just worked, which led to investigating why
As it turns out, fasting has amazing benefits, even for just hours a day, giving your body a break from digesting food
Your testosterone immediately goes down when you eat, so intermittent fasting is incredibly powerful for supporting and boosting your hormones
Digestion is really the biggest energy draw on your body: it takes tremendous energy
Energy went up tremendously once fasting was part of the daily routine
Personally, the benefits of intermittent fasting are really wide and varied: more energy, a simpler life with fewer meals, putting on muscle and keeping off fat easier
Personally, everything about a shorter eating window has been incredibly beneficial
If there's one thing nutritionally to try, it's intermittent fasting
There's so much science now on intermittent fasting, but the bottom line: "Intermittent fasting just works", and it will probably, honestly, benefit your life
Ease into intermittent fasting gradually, so your body adapts
Eating now typically happens in about a two- to four-hour period each day, a fast of 20 to 22 hours
A personal two- to four-hour eating period is not a suggestion to jump at once from eating from breakfast until evening to only two or four hours
Eating from soon after waking until later, you're really not fasting except while you sleep
The best start to intermittent fasting is cutting out breakfast: you're already fasting from the evening, so start eating at noonish, with lunch, for at least a few hours in a true fasting state
When fasting, it takes about 12 hours for your body to kind of shift gears into certain really beneficial processes
Stop eating at 7 p.m. and eat breakfast at 7 or 8 a.m., and you start eating just as the amazing benefits of fasting would begin
Skipping breakfast gives you at least a few hours a day past the 12-hour point of fasting, enough to start feeling the benefits
A promise: you'll adapt to fasting quicker, and probably more easily, than you think
For a lot of people used to eating basically all their waking hours, fasting can seem kind of rough, but your body will adapt
The next step in intermittent fasting is your eating window: from when you start eating until you stop for the day
Breakfast by 8 a.m. and eating until 8 p.m., hopefully not later, is a 12-hour eating window
Cut your eating window back more and more for more benefit: in personal experience, the shorter the window, the better the results
If there's one other thing to avoid food-wise, it's eating really late at night: it hurts your hormones and kills your morning wood

section: What to eat in the window
claim: One caveat to the eating window: still pay attention to what you fuel with during your window, especially as you cut it shorter, if you go that way

section: What to eat in the window
claim: During your eating window, eat effectively, the right mix to support your activity and body

section: What to eat in the window
claim: With a shorter eating window and training really hard, you sometimes have to really pay attention to eating enough

section: What to eat in the window
claim: Not training super hard and maybe trying to keep extra weight off, paying attention to what you fuel with in your eating window can still mean watching that you maybe don't eat too much, or some of the junkier things

section: What to eat in the window
claim: The eating window is amazingly powerful, but not a complete magic bullet: four hours a day of fast food, and you're screwed

section: What to eat in the window
claim: With an eating window, the fundamentals of eating good fuel still apply
Intermittent fasting is so powerful for how you feel, burning fat, keeping your metabolism up, your energy levels and building muscle really easily
Intermittent fasting works especially well for men, though it does work well for women also
If you haven't tried intermittent fasting, it very potentially could change your life from a nutritional fuel standpoint, so working towards it is highly encouraged
To try intermittent fasting, skip breakfast every day for a week and see how you feel and how long you take to adapt
Over time, in general, the shorter and earlier in the day your eating window, the better you'll feel
